name: round 2: struct per lane, u32 output
why: the struct stays in workgroup memory; only one field is stored to a u32 buffer

name: round 2: u32 per lane, struct output
why: a u32 in workgroup memory; the result is stored as a whole struct

name: round 2: vec4<u32> per lane and output
why: no struct anywhere: a vec4<u32> in workgroup memory and as output

name: round 2: struct per lane read field by field
why: the struct in workgroup memory is never copied whole: each field is read on its own

name: round 2: struct per lane stored field by field
why: the struct is copied whole from workgroup memory, but stored to the buffer one field at a time

name: round 2: struct per lane, no loop
why: a struct in workgroup memory written, one barrier, the neighbour's read and stored whole; no reduction loop

name: round 3: struct array of 512
why: the struct array in workgroup memory is twice the workgroup size, so the read can never pass its end

name: round 3: struct array of 258
why: the struct array is two longer than the workgroup; the read can still pass its end

name: round 3: struct read downward
why: the struct array of the workgroup's size read at lid - (1 << i) under lid >= (1 << i), the way backdrop does

name: round 3: struct, no input read
why: the struct kernel with the lane's own index as its input, no storage buffer read
